## Overview


Modify Dockerfile to include SM107a in the DeepEP section. Guarded by flag INSTALL_RUBIN_PRERELEASE
## Validation


This change helps pass some unit test like:

- tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py::test_moe_layer[False-deepep_high_throughput-2-1-True]

- tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py::test_moe_layer[False-deepep_low_latency-2-1-True]

I think there might be an issue, it seems like DeepEP builds through torch.utils.cpp_extension, this file has a list of predefined Archs https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/146a5a2f73e2980170c08e5bb6d0c7ffb703f7de/torch/utils/cpp_extension.py#L2814 , that can lead to ```ValueError: Unknown CUDA arch (10.0f) or GPU not supported```
I guess we need to be explicit and use 10.7a

inline_comments.body: Just out of curiosity. Is there any explanation why we have to build DeepEP wheel ourselves? This is a general question, it does not depend specifically on architecture.

My guess is the commit and nvshmem version:
```
/tmp/install_python_libraries.sh \
        --workspace /tmp/ep_kernels_workspace \
        --mode wheel \
        ${DEEPEP_COMMIT_HASH:+--deepep-ref "$DEEPEP_COMMIT_HASH"} \
        ${NVSHMEM_VER:+--nvshmem-ver "$NVSHMEM_VER"} && \
```

Unfortunate. I'm checking the binary size of building for all three blackwell kernels now. Perhaps we should just remove the `a` and build for `10.0`

Note that it appears this only affects the legacy V1 DeepEP kernels, since DeepEPv2 is jitted.
